C-GUARD-RATCHET.IntentSummary:
Author the execution for the approved, fingerprinted spec `.ngrace/changes/active/C-GUARD-RATCHET/spec.xml` (ratified `approved`, gate permit and spec fingerprint `8e8acc00faf28f6313756cc65b272d06636398d98bca725493c8c59a8deb4f9b` recorded in the bundle's `run-ledger.xml`, commit `9171fe6` on `c-guard-ratchet`) and only within it; the plan conforms to the spec, it does not extend, narrow or reinterpret it. The spec fixes the six-entry flush, the forced mid-bundle move, `D39`'s boundary statement and `F223`'s early exit, `D39`'s codification as the authority's close act, the write scope, the criterion mapping, and the faithful post-close copy — this plan takes all of that from the spec.
Three tasks carry the committed sequence. T-001 is the spec's sequence step (1) and the `AC-PAYMENTS-LANDED`-shaped instrument: the red-first `C-GUARD-RATCHET` walk, the five findings and `D39` with their six index `Entry` lines, `F244`'s append to the already-archived `C-PAYMENT-INTEGRITY` row, the born-live `C-GUARD-RATCHET` row, the shipped `--rewrite-roots`, the declared mid-state (validator exit 1, one finding), one `--retire` (`moved 1`), and the two suite repairs the moved state forces. T-002 is the spec's sequence step (2): `src/artifact/xml.test.ts` gains the two red-first self-directed directions, the threat-model/boundary docblock paragraph, and the split early exit. T-003 is verification and the post-close reachability drive: the leaf suites, `bun run validate:ci`, the byte-invariance diffs, the F242 typecheck count for the one touched `scripts/` file, the `approved`-copy anchors-window confirmation, and the faithful post-close drive that reaches the state the ceremony produces.
**The close is the authority's act and this plan's tasks end before it.** Execution ends when T-003 is verified and its cursor events are recorded; no task performs `terminal`, `fold`, `review`, the verdict, `gate apply`, `gate archive`, `ngrace apply`, `D39`'s `CodifiedIn` hand write, the close's `--retire`, any `CloseEvidence` run, or the post-archive verdict. Which task leaves each close-needed piece in place: T-001 leaves `D39` live in `rulings.xml` with its single live index `Entry` (so the close can hand-write the `CodifiedIn` onto it), leaves `F222`, `F223` and the `C-GUARD-RATCHET` row live (so the close's move takes four), and leaves the record validating clean; T-002 leaves `src/artifact/xml.test.ts` at 37 pass / 0 fail; T-003 records every cursor event, drives every `CloseEvidence` command and `validate:ci` inside a faithful post-close copy, and leaves the production bundle active, its plan still `draft`, no status hand-written and no directory moved. The close then runs `lint --assertions final --run-commands` with the record still clean, `ngrace apply` (which writes `applied` and renames the bundle into `.ngrace/changes/archive/`), then hand-writes `<CodifiedIn kind="test-suite">src/artifact/xml.test.ts</CodifiedIn>` on the now-applied `D39` (the `C-APPLY-VERB` close `ba148c0` is the precedent for that order), then runs its own `--retire` (expected `moved 4` — `F222`, `F223`, `D39` and the row), then evaluates the `CloseEvidence`. No sentence in this plan implies execution performs any of those.
**The mid-bundle red is a task's act and a declared working-tree state, never a commit.** Inside T-001, after the hand writes and `--rewrite-roots` and before the move, the shipped `bun ./scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts` exits 1 naming exactly one entry: `F244` (archive event `C-PAYMENT-INTEGRITY`). That is the D28.1 enforcement saying the move is due — a declared, verified working-tree state `validate:ci` can never see, because the same task's next act is the move and the commit holds only the moved state. One `bun ./scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts --retire docs/plans/active/RM-GOVERNED-PATH` reports `moved 1`; the validator then exits 0. No task boundary and no recorded `Verification` command sits inside the red window. Which entries move when: mid-bundle, `F244`; at the close (the authority's), `F222`, `F223`, `D39`, and the `C-GUARD-RATCHET` row. Nothing else in the findings, rulings, registry or index genres moves.
**Two honest reds by construction, planned as fail→pass pairs with keys.** (1) T-001 adds the `C-GUARD-RATCHET` carrier-and-row walk to `scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts` **before any record write**, and drives it: red on the production record, 101 pass / 2 fail (the new `describe` is 0 pass / 2 fail — the production relation reads no row and the red fixture's "the mutated copy carries two `C-GUARD-RATCHET` rows" precondition fails); the writes, the move and the repairs are the pass, 103 pass / 0 fail. Signature-kind `test`, key `cgr-carrier-row-walk-first`. (2) T-002 adds the guard's two self-directed directions **before** the docblock and the split early exit land, and drives them: red, 35 pass / 2 fail (both new directions fail — the docblock lacks the statement and `visitSubtree` has no early exit); the docblock and the split early exit are the pass, 37 pass / 0 fail. Signature-kind `test`, key `guard-directions-first`. The mid-state validator red is the D28.1 enforcement, not a cycle, and is not counted as an attempt.
**Why three tasks and not fewer or more.** The fix budgets bind per task (`src/grace-cursor.ts:187` `FIX_SIGNATURE_REPEAT_BUDGET = 2`; `src/grace-cursor.ts:193` `FIX_DISTINCT_SIGNATURE_BUDGET = 4`, both re-read at this plan's commit `9171fe6`). T-001's failure-signature families are the walk authoring (the planned pair), the record hand writes and the root read-back, the move's report, and the two suite repairs — four distinct, inside the per-task distinct budget of 4, with the same-signature repeat budget of 2. T-002's families are the two directions (the planned pair) and the guard edits — two distinct. T-003 is verification and the post-close drive, not a write task; its commands mutate only a throwaway copy, and its one planned failure signature is the post-close drive itself. Folding T-002 into T-001 would put two independent write families (the record with the engine's suite, and the guard's `src/` test) in one task's budget for no gain; splitting T-003 is impossible because the post-close drive needs every earlier task landed.
**The committed state machine, driven end to end on whole-repository copies at this plan's commit** (every exit code read directly; the copies are `/tmp/ng-plan/repo` for the post-move/target state, `/tmp/ng-plan/redonly` for T-001's red-first state, `/tmp/ng-plan/guard2` for T-002's green state, and the post-close copy named by T-003). Baseline `fa1773d` + `9171fe6`: findings `7569 / 266 / 7835`, rulings `1733 / 150 / 1883`, registry `12 / 14 / 26`, index `270 / 26 / 296`; the retirement suite is 101 pass / 0 fail; `src/artifact/xml.test.ts` is 35 pass / 0 fail; the record validators exit 0. T-001's boundary: findings `7668 / 167 / 7835`, rulings `1760 / 123 / 1883`, registry `13 / 13 / 26`, index `275 / 21 / 296`; validator exit 0; suite 103 pass / 0 fail. T-002's boundary: `src/artifact/xml.test.ts` 37 pass / 0 fail; the retirement suite unchanged at 103 / 0. T-003: `bun run validate:ci` exit 0 in tree. The close: `ngrace apply` archives the bundle, `D39`'s `CodifiedIn` is hand-written, the close's `--retire` reports `moved 4`, findings `7595 / 240 / 7835`, rulings `1733 / 150 / 1883`, registry `12 / 14 / 26`, index `272 / 24 / 296`; `F244` retired `<PaidBy>C-PAYMENT-INTEGRITY</PaidBy>`, `F222` and `F223` retired `<PaidBy>C-GUARD-RATCHET</PaidBy>`, `D39` retired in `rulings-retired.xml` carrying its resolving `CodifiedIn`, the row retired in `registry-retired.xml`; every `CloseEvidence` command and `bun run validate:ci` exit 0.
**The two suite repairs are exactly the two the spec forces, and no shipped assertion outside them is rewritten.** (1) The `bundleMinted` extension in the `C-RECORD-PARSE payer derivation` test gains `F244: "C-PAYMENT-INTEGRITY"`, `F222: "C-GUARD-RATCHET"` and `F223: "C-GUARD-RATCHET"`; the extension is consulted only for tokens the derivation actually mints, so the walk is green before the payments too. (2) The `C-PAYMENT-INTEGRITY` carrier list gains `F244: "C-PAYMENT-INTEGRITY"`, and that walk's `Pays exactly "F197"` clause becomes the payment-invariant containment form (Pays names `F197` / `F198`); an exact set expires on the next lawful retired-row append (`F225`/`F238`'s class), and the drive proves it: with the append and without the repair the post-close suite is 99 pass / 2 fail (`C-RECORD-PARSE payer derivation`; `C-PAYMENT-INTEGRITY carrier and row relations`, `Expected: "F197" / Received: "F197 F244"`), and with both repairs it is 103 pass / 0 fail. `F244` owes no code — the clamp test it records is already gone at this commit (deleted by `C-PAYMENT-INTEGRITY`) — only the payment record above.
**The F242 typecheck count and the anchors window, measured at this plan's commit.** The touched `scripts/` file is not under `tsconfig.json`'s `src/**` include, so `bun run typecheck` never reads it (F242). Driven with `bunx tsc --noEmit --ignoreConfig --strict --types bun-types --moduleResolution bundler --allowImportingTsExtensions scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts` → 3 errors at `:2589`, `:3773`, `:4034` (the `toBe(string | undefined)` overload class F242 records), before and expected unchanged after; this bundle fixes none of them. No `src/` file is created and `src/artifact/xml.test.ts` is lint-checked at every state; at `approved` on a copy the `M-GRAMMAR` `DurableScope` over a `.test.ts` write raises no `change.graph-anchors-miss-write-scope` (a `.test.ts` is not module-ownable), confirmed by T-003's drive.
The mapping, fixed by the spec's own Constraint. Exactly one criterion — `AC-NO-CURRENT-MODE` — carries no `CloseEvidence` and must be mapped by exactly one task `Satisfies`; it is carried by T-003, this plan's only `Satisfies`. The other eleven criteria are close-bound and stay unmapped, because a `Satisfies` of a close-bound criterion is the shipped error `change.close-evidence-and-satisfied` (`src/lint/catalog.ts:286`), and an unmapped non-CloseEvidence criterion is the warning `AC-CLOSE-LINT`'s `--fail-on warnings` turns into an uncloseable bundle. Every `CloseEvidence` is evaluated only in the applied-archive state (`F196`'s rule), so T-003 writes its drive against the state the ceremony produces, never the pre-close tree.

The red-direction fixture copies all seven record files it reads into an isolated root, plants a duplicate row into whichever layer holds it (verifying the mutation landed before reading the result, `F229`/`F237`'s state-independent form), and asserts the exactly-once clause throws; a fixture that copies only a subset ENOENTs, so the copy list names every file the relation reads. Then run the shipped writer `bun ./scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts --rewrite-roots` — never hand-edit a root; the roots read back findings `7694 / 141 / 7835`, rulings `1760 / 123 / 1883`, index `276 / 20 / 296`, registry `13 / 13 / 26` (driven). T-002.Title: Add the guard's two red-first self-directed directions, then state its threat model and known boundary in the docblock and land the split early exit in visitSubtree

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: The docblock statement, exact. The `antiOccupancyFailures` docblock gains, after the existing `Shapes the scan cannot prove are reported, never passed.` sentence, the paragraph the spec's exact-bytes Constraint pins: the guard's threat model is accidental drift — the next flush re-pinning a count as a literal, restoring an occupancy table, or adding a module-scope constant — and its known boundary is the eight deliberate constructions, by shape, named as outside the charter. No duty is widened; no supersede of `C-FLUSH-AND-PAY-3` is opened; no ninth construction is asserted. Escape markup as character data in every written cell.

The early exit, split and no behavioural change. `visitSubtree` becomes: `if (visit(node) === true) return true;` then `return ts.forEachChild(node, (child) => visitSubtree(child, visit));`, with the signature `(node: ts.Node, visit: (child: ts.Node) => boolean | void): boolean | undefined`, so the `true` propagates through `ts.forEachChild` and siblings after the found node are not visited. `pairingCallbackBody`'s shipped combined guard `if (found !== undefined || !ts.isCallExpression(node)) return;` is split into `if (found !== undefined) return true;` then `if (!ts.isCallExpression(node)) return;`, and the callback ends `found = callback.body; return true;` — a node that is not an `it` call still returns void and the walk continues. Every other `visitSubtree` caller returns void, so its traversal is unchanged. Driven: the two directions pass, 37 pass / 0 fail; the guard's pre-existing directions are 35 pass / 0 fail before and after, and the control mutation (`expected: number` as a real interface member) still fires, 34 pass / 1 fail; the split form alone (no new tests) is 35 pass / 0 fail with the control at 34 pass / 1 fail. The retirement suite is unchanged at 103 pass / 0 fail. This task's failure-signature families are the two directions (the planned pair) and the guard edits — two distinct, inside the per-task distinct budget of 4 (`src/grace-cursor.ts:193`), with the same-signature repeat budget of 2 (`:187`).

The boundary and the close. This task's `Verification` commands and the plan's `TargetAssertions` contain no current-mode lint of this project root, checked by hand (F171). Each recorded command exits 0 at this task's boundary (F184), driven on the faithful copy at exactly this stage; each `git diff --exit-code` names the base commit `fa1773d7b853050d2330e4aa21f0514c3e8d6b05` and excludes both this task's and the earlier task's files (F243). `src/artifact/xml.test.ts` is lint-checked at every state (`src/` is not lint-ignored). No `src/` runtime file is created or edited, so no `change.graph-anchors-miss-write-scope` window exists; the `M-GRAMMAR` `DurableScope` is the test surface's owning anchor. The executor emits its own cursor events and performs no close act; the close remains the authority's.
